# Known, accepted failures of the nightly forecast refresh.
#
# The scheduled run exits non-zero whenever anything breaches, and that is
# correct -- the build status should honestly say "something is breaching".
# But an alarm that opens an issue every night for the same known thing is one
# people learn to ignore, which is the failure this repo's own workflow
# comments were written to prevent.
#
# So the alarm fires on a CHANGE. Every token below is a failure someone has
# looked at and decided to live with, for a reason recorded here. Anything NOT
# in this list raises the alarm.
#
# Tokens come from scripts/failure_signature.sh and carry what and who, never
# how much, so a moving number does not read as a new problem:
#
#   stage:<script or stage name>
#   breach:<CODE>:<cycle year>:<party>
#
# ADDING A LINE HERE IS A DECISION, NOT HOUSEKEEPING. It means "we know, and
# the alarm should stop telling us". Say why, and say what would make it
# removable. A line with no reason is indistinguishable from a silenced bug.
#
# REMOVE a line the moment its failure is fixed. A stale entry here is worse
# than no baseline: it would mute the failure if it ever came back. The alarm
# step reports tokens that are in this file but no longer failing, so the
# run summary will tell you when one is ready to delete.

# --- NSW 2027 One Nation, poll tracking ------------------------------------
# fit_nsw.R's NL3 check: One Nation is fitted below its own recent polls by
# more than the 2.5-point bound. Partial pooling of thin parties' walk
# parameters (AUSPOL_NSW_THIN_WALK, shipped 2026-09-14) narrowed the gap from
# 5.15 to 3.38 but did not close it.
#
# Kept rather than fixed because two pre-registered experiments aborted on
# whether the gap is the fit or the check, the second at 19 cycles against a
# floor of 20 -- see docs/plans/prereg-poll-tracking-bound-scaling.md, whose
# closing section records that the remaining options are decisions rather than
# experiments and forbids raising POLL_TRACKING_BOUND or min_polls to clear it.
#
# REMOVABLE WHEN: the separability gate can run (it needs one more completed
# election with polls), or Pete decides between the options that plan names.
#
# NOTE the shape of the middle line. It was `stage:fit_nsw.R` until review on
# 2026-09-14 pointed out that such a token matches that script failing for ANY
# reason -- so a brand-new NL4 breach, or an unrelated crash, would have been
# muted by an entry whose justification above is specifically about NL3 and One
# Nation. Carrying the reason means a different failure in the same script is a
# different token, and therefore an alarm.
#
# So do NOT shorten these lines to make them tidy. The detail is the point.
stage:NSW cycles
stage:fit_nsw.R:CHECK:NL3 breached on 1 NSW cycle(s) -- details above and in outpu
breach:NL3:2027:ONP
